items.title: [wildcard] Zero-copy loan slices across the assembly trampoline via static GC-pin certificates

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Eliminate serialization and buffer-copy overhead across the Go-to-Rust assembly trampoline (call_sysv.s / call_win64.s) by letting hy-check's existing loan checker (SPEC-LANGUAGE.md §9) issue static stack-bound pin certificates for borrowed slices (&[]byte, &string). Currently, crossing into the Rust staticlib (serde_json, regex, sha3) requires copying payload bytes or marshaling across the bridge because Go's GC moving/stack-shrinking semantics forbid raw pointer retention across arbitrary calls. However, because Hybrid's assembly trampoline executes synchronously on a switched system stack with bounded two-tier budgets (Spike 1 & Spike 4) and cannot trigger a Go stack growth on the caller frame while suspended, any non-escaping loan proven exclusive by Tier-0 can be passed as a raw {ptr, len} fat pointer directly into Rust  &[u8] with zero allocation and zero copying.

### Which assumption it breaks

Breaks the assumption in Spike 1 / G2 and SPEC-LANGUAGE.md that the Go-to-Rust staticlib bridge must treat slice/string arguments as value-copied or opaque ABI buffers to preserve Go GC invariants. It merges Tier-0 static loan lifetimes (hy-check) directly with the low-level assembly trampoline ABI (hy-emit + runtime/).

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

While Spike 1 reduced call overhead from 46.8 ns (cgo) to 3.37 ns via stack-switched assembly trampolines, that 16.5x win only applies to fixed-size scalar arguments; real-world workloads (serde_json parsing 64 KB payloads or sha3 hashing buffers) immediately lose that advantage to O(N) memory copying across the boundary. Proving that Tier-0 exclusive loans mathematically guarantee pointer stability during synchronous trampoline execution turns Hybrid's ownership checker from a purely defensive safety tool into a zero-copy performance weapon that beats handwritten cgo on throughput, not just call latency.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Falsifiable Metric: Benchmark sha3 and serde_json bridge crossings on 1 KiB, 64 KiB, and 1 MiB payloads using borrowed &[]byte fat-pointer views vs. current bridge lowering; throughput must improve by >=3x on >=64 KiB payloads with 0 B/op and 0 allocs/op under go test -bench and clean execution under -race + GODEBUG=gcstoptheworld=1 / stack-move stress tests (runtime.GC()).

Defeat Condition: If Go 1.26.9's concurrent mark/sweep or stack shrinking can relocate a stack-allocated backing array of a slice while its goroutine is parked on the assembly trampoline stack switch without runtime. Pinner overhead, or if pinning costs exceed the O(N) copy time for payloads under 16 KiB, the zero copy static loan assumption is falsified.
Settlement Wallet (Base USDC): 0xefC7eC8C30c29e2f48810A5b0AB0693DA3DFcc6e

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

Static proof holds trivially for heap-backed slices under Go's non-moving heap collector, but stack-allocated backing arrays require proving the goroutine stack cannot shrink while parked across the assembly trampoline boundary; if false, the compiler must force escape-to-heap on bridge loaned slices.

### Track terms

- [x] I understand no prototype is required and failure-with-knowledge is a valid, paid outcome
- [x] I understand all outcomes (including declines and failures) are published in MOONSHOT.md

items.title: [wildcard] Certified Task-Region Memory Budgets: compile-time static max-RSS certificates

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Introduce static task memory budgeting (task(budget = 16.MiB) worker()) certified by an allocation-effect contract at compile time. Currently, Hybrid proves data-race freedom across tasks (GUARANTEES.md Row 1) and memory safety via Go's GC (Row 17), but explicitly makes zero claims about memory exhaustion (OOM), task leak budgets, or allocation bounds. By coupling the escape analysis of hy-check with an affine capability-bounded allocation budget, every spawned task carries an allocation certificate verified against its static call graph. If a task cannot be bounded, it must either be marked unbounded (task(budget = unmetered)) or routed through an isolated arena/slab allocator that fails gracefully (or cancels the task scope) instead of killing the entire Go process via OS OOM.

### Which assumption it breaks

Kills the sacred cow in GUARANTEES.md Row 17 (Memory safety, Go side: Go's GC, unchanged - Hybrid emits Go source): breaks the assumption that Go's runtime GC alone is sufficient for robust concurrent services. Extends Tier-0 to verify capacity bounds in addition to dataflow. Challenges unconstrained goroutine emission in hy-emit.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Normal feature bounties optimize existing AST lowering or catch compiler bugs in the current shape. This proposal addresses the single largest operational failure mode of concurrent Go services in production: runaway goroutines accumulating heap memory until the kernel OOM killer terminates the container. Hybrid already possesses the exact machinery needed to fix this—its linear loan checker, escape-path tracker, and composite ownership model (Section 9.3). Turning those flow proofs into an upper-bound memory certificate turns Hybrid from 'Go with data-race checks' into 'Go with mission-critical bounded execution guarantees'.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

1. Falsifiable Metric: Formulate allocation-cost model in hy-check. For streaming fan-out with 10k tasks, hyb check computes an upper-bound footprint within 15% of measured heap delta under runtime.ReadMemStats(). 2. Defeat Condition: If recursion or foreign Go calls degrade static upper bound to Infinity on >40% of non-trivial code, static approach is falsified and pivots to explicit bounded runtime arenas with ErrTaskMemoryExceeded. Settlement Wallet (Base USDC): 0x7Fc0F41448f8e6622487Bc31cAa7a692c2777a71

_No response_

items.title: [wildcard] Make hy-check an untrusted proof producer: permission certificates for actual Go

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

For an opt-in certified subset, make neither `hy-check` nor `hy-emit` trusted for the emitted artifact's race-freedom claim. They produce Go plus a candidate permission derivation; an independent kernel checks that derivation against the **actual typed Go CFG**, including allocations, aliases, reads/writes and spawn/send transfers. A frontend ACCEPT or a certificate merely asserting ‘sendable’ is not evidence. The research question is whether explicit proof checking can remove inference/search from the trusted safety core without becoming another full checker.

### Which assumption it breaks

Challenge trusting `hy-check`'s implementation for the certified artifact's safety. At inspected main `1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b`, [stmt.rs:39–69](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/compiler/crates/hy-emit/src/stmt.rs#L39) intentionally erases move markers and emits ordinary Go sends/goroutines. That is not a bug report. Could the resulting artifact instead carry independently checked safety evidence even when inference is wrong?

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

- [W-013/#345](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/345) explicitly **keeps hy-check trusted** and verifies checked-IR-to-Go preservation. Here the checker is also an untrusted proof producer; the target is a direct safety property of actual Go.
- [W-004/#174](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/174) relies on phantom witnesses and `cmd/compile`. This kernel would check permission/alias derivations for supported storage and reject unsupported captures; ordinary Go type-checking alone cannot certify it.
- [W-023/#565](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/565) uses toolchain/test oracles. Finitely many successful executions are not a proof derivation.

Proof-carrying code is established work, not a claimed invention here. The bounded tracker searches did not identify this same trust-boundary change; they are not an exhaustive novelty proof. If maintainers group it with an existing family, shared evaluation or decline is preferable to duplicate work.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

**Initial boundary:** a closed program with scalar inputs and internally allocated storage. Support scalars, slices of scalars with explicit backing roots, static callees, branches, and one-way spawn/send ownership transfer. Borrowed mutable entry inputs, mutable globals, loops, defer/panic/recover, closures, maps, FFI, managed code, unsafe, reflection and unresolved dispatch initially receive no certificate. Calls require a checked callee derivation in the same closed artifact.

**Obligation:** cover every actual CFG edge and memory operation. Reference copies retain their backing-root identity; only a checked allocation rule creates freshness. Write permission cannot be duplicated among concurrently live tasks. Check join assertions rather than trust them. Bind the proof to the full Go input set actually compiled, build tags/platform/toolchain configuration, checked callee derivations, semantics and kernel version.

| Proposed falsifier/control | Required outcome |
|---|---|
| Supported spawn/send with actual reads/writes and uniquely transferred storage | Accept |
| Surviving-alias writes after transfer; overlapping concurrent slice writes | Reject |
| Forged freshness/sendable labels, omitted CFG edges, unsafe type-correct output mutations | Reject independently of hy-check |
| Unsupported constructs, changed artifact, incomplete derivation | No certificate |
| Race-free but functionally wrong output | May pass safety; must still fail the separate behaviour gate |

An illustrative in-subset negative case (not run) is `x := make([]int, 2); alias := x[:1]; go write(x); alias[0] = 1`, with a statically known `write` that mutates the overlapping element. The kernel must reject this even with forged permission annotations; rejection must not merely rely on an unsupported closure or foreign feature.

Before prototyping, publish the exact case/mutation inventory and trust ledger. Proposed budget: at most **2,000 non-generated semantic-rule LOC**, locally checked rule/dataflow replay only (no global invariant or proof search), and no new SMT-solver trust. List Go frontend dependencies separately and compare both designs on **the same admitted features**; shrinking the language is not itself a trust reduction.

Reject or narrow the thesis if meaningful positive cases cannot be certified, unsafe variants pass, permissions still depend on trusted hy-check labels, the kernel copies the existing search engine, or added dependencies defeat the trust reduction.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

A restricted-Go semantics, proof format, producer and independent verifier may cost more than they save. Go parsing/type resolution, kernel rules, and the Go compiler/runtime remain trust assumptions. A toy safe subset is not a convincing success.

This certifies neither source equivalence nor business-result correctness, foreign code, or arbitrary Go. Those separate obligations remain. Existing semantics and the native backend must not silently weaken.

If selected, M1 is this written hypothesis and falsification plan; M2 publishes an accept/narrow/reject learning and trust/scope ledger, with illustrative arguments distinguished from experimental evidence. Any execution gets a separately preregistered scope. **No prototype, tests, benchmark or formal safety result has been produced.**

One wildcard winner is selected per cycle. Submission, acknowledgement or a ledger slot is not an award or receivable.

Sources reviewed at the inspected commit: [BOUNTY.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/BOUNTY.md), [MOONSHOT.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/MOONSHOT.md), [GUARANTEES.md](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/1f0ff978f4deff78c77bca96db0e3e46f32de71b/GUARANTEES.md), README, AGENTS, the wildcard template, and the linked related proposals.

items.title: Serial by default: safe execution first

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

In an opt-in closed fork-join scope, make task execution safe by default. Rather than reject tasks whenever shared-data independence cannot be proved, the compiler orders possibly conflicting tasks sequentially. It runs tasks in parallel only when it can prove their data accesses are independent. Unknown means slower, not unsafe.

### Which assumption it breaks

Break the assumption that developers must prove sendability/ownership at every task boundary to make useful concurrent code compile. For a new closed scope, concurrency becomes an optimization, not an admission condition. If the scope's mutable state could escape to other goroutines, reject it.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Instead of 'prove concurrency safety first or fail', Hybrid could offer 'run correctly first, accelerate automatically'. This is not STM: no speculative writes, retries or rollback. It is not full object cloning or fixed-rate synchronous dataflow. Conflicts are ordered before work begins; only independent tasks run together.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Prototype two-task fork-join regions. Test same-map writes serialize and pass go test -race; proven independent roots overlap in time; ambiguous accesses serialize; an escaped reference is rejected; a blocking receive is rejected before scheduling. Measure overhead versus regular Hybrid. Fail the hypothesis if ownership isolation requires rebuilding the full alias checker or serial overhead is excessive.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

Requires opt-in syntax, whole-region ownership checks, conservative read/write effect summaries, dependency-DAG scheduling and new diagnostics. First version excludes dynamic spawn, uncontrolled I/O, blocking calls and escaped references. Existing task semantics remain unchanged. AI-assisted proposal; no prototype or benchmarks claimed.

items.title: [wildcard] Structured Task Scopes & Affine Cancellation Tokens: eliminating goroutine leaks from GUARANTEES.md Row 12

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

items.body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Introduce lexically-bounded Structured Task Scopes (`scope { ... }` blocks) and Affine Cancellation Tokens into Hybrid, elevating concurrency from uncoordinated "fire-and-forget" spawns to compile-time-guaranteed lifetime containment. Today, `task` spawns an unjoined goroutine with zero lifetime binding to its caller; if a context cancels or the caller returns early, the child task becomes a silent orphan, leaking memory and holding open channels or locks. We propose making every `task` spawned within a `scope` yield an affine `JoinHandle[T]`. A `scope` block cannot exit until all child handles are joined, cancelled, or drained. Unjoined task handles trigger compile-time diagnostic `HYB-E3501 (unjoined task escape)`. This directly flips GUARANTEES.md Row 12 from "no claim about cancellation semantics" into a provable compile-time invariant: Zero Orphan Tasks, Zero Goroutine Leaks, and Complete Structured Concurrency in the checked subset.

Settlement EVM Wallet (USDC Base/EVM): 0x3a5E08708dd1CF22AAe94f913Ab69b17b80a3dC5

### Which assumption it breaks

1. It breaks GUARANTEES.md Row 12 ("context.Context cancellation trees — No claim about cancellation semantics; the claim is about value sharing, not protocol liveness").
2. It kills the sacred cow that Hybrid concurrency must compile down to naked, unmanaged `go func()` invocations.
3. It challenges the assumption that lifetime analysis is strictly for memory references, proving that task execution lifetimes can be checked using the existing borrow-checker loan/alias infrastructure without dynamic GC overhead.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

In standard Go, goroutine leaks caused by lost context cancellations are notoriously the #1 source of production memory bloat and deadlocks. Ordinary Go cannot enforce structured concurrency because `go` statements are inherently unstructured primitives. 

Hybrid has already solved compile-time data race freedom via ownership and sendability; by solving compile-time structured concurrency and leak-freedom, Hybrid becomes the first language in the Go ecosystem to deliver Nathaniel J. Smith / Martin Sustrik-style structured concurrency completely verified at compile time with zero runtime penalty. It transforms Hybrid from merely "race-free Go" into "leak-free, crash-resilient Go".

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

1. Milestone M1 (Acceptance & Formal Specification): Define the AST grammar for `scope { ... }` and affine `JoinHandle[T]`, and document the formal typing rule in SPEC-LANGUAGE.md showing how early scope returns force compile-time join checks.
2. Milestone M2 (Corpus Evaluation & Falsification): Implement an adversarial test corpus of 25 canonical leaky Go patterns (timeout leaks, select default bypasses, panic escapes). The checker must successfully reject 100% of unjoined escape paths while lowering clean scopes to zero-allocation inlined `sync.WaitGroup` code. A documented post-mortem on whether foreign Go API callbacks break this boundary satisfies the M2 learning deliverable.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

1. Language Surface: Requires adding `scope` keyword or block syntax to `hy-check` and threading an affine lifetime tracker through the loan analysis table.
2. Migration & Backwards Compatibility: Legacy top-level `task` spawns would need a transitional `detached task` keyword or deprecation lint to avoid breaking existing MVP test suites.
3. Foreign Boundary: Tasks spawned inside foreign Go callbacks (`net/http`) cannot be statically enclosed by a Hybrid scope, which must remain an explicit managed escape hatch.
